input.quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
input.rationale: Section 20 meets the preferred position. Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer and its Affiliates for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims (20.1) and for Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud (20.2). Standard procedure (prompt notice, cooperation at indemnifier's expense, control of defence, prejudice-based delay carve-out, settlement consent) appears in 20.4, and the procure/modify/replace/refund remedies in 20.5 are additive to the defence obligation. Customer's indemnity is appropriately narrow — limited to unmodified Customer-supplied material and Customer's violation of Applicable Law, with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modifications, combinations and Vendor instructions (20.3). Indemnification obligations are "Excluded Claims" under 21.3, so the Vendor indemnity sits outside the liability cap (better than the fallback super-cap). No redline required.
